newsitem.title: ITALY: Market expectations increase for Italian rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Market expectations increase for Italian rate cut.

text.p: Expectations of an interest rate cut by the Bank of Italy increased this week as the money market on Friday signalled the overnight rate would fall over the next month below the current 7.50 official discount rate.

A weekly study based on implicit rates compiled by Bocconi University's research department Igier for Reuters showed the implicit overnight rate on a one-month horizon at 7.23 percent, down from a market close of 7.63 percent on Thursday, the day on which Igier conducted its study.
Last week's Igier study saw the implicit overnight rate falling within a month to 7.51 percent. Four weeks ago it predicted a fall within one month to 7.43 percent.
On a three month timeframe the implicit overnight rate was seen in the latest study at 6.63 percent, down from 6.79 percent seen a week ago and 6.84 percent a month ago.

On a one-year horizon, the implicit overnight rate was seen falling to 5.94 percent from 6.02 percent a week ago and 6.06 percent one month ago. On a two-year time frame the implicit overnight rate was seen at 6.65 percent from 6.80 percent a week ago and 6.73 percent a month ago.

The spread between the implicit Italian overnight rate and the implicit German overnight rate, considered a good indicator of market confidence in Europe's economic and monetary union, was seen at 194 basis points from 207 basis points last week and 180 bps two weeks ago.
